rules.description: A node's children are distinct: achieving or addressing one does not achieve or address another

semantic.rubric: Judge the item's children as a set. If the criterion names a kind of child, judge only those and ignore the rest. The children are distinct when each is a different need, result or idea, so that achieving or addressing one does not achieve or address another.

overlapping.description: Two children state the same thing, or partly cover the same ground, or one contains another
overlapping.guidance: Merge them, sharpen the boundary between them, or nest the narrower one under the broader one.

rules.description: Together, a node's children cover what it needs

semantic.rubric: Judge the item's children as a set. If the criterion names a kind of child, judge only those and ignore the rest. Pass when achieving all of them would achieve the item as its title and body state it. Fail when a part that the item names or plainly needs has no child.

rules.description: A node belongs under its parent: it is one part, cause, case or means of the parent

semantic.rubric: Judge only how the item relates to its parent. Something worthwhile in the same area as the parent does not refine the parent unless it passes the criterion's test.

verdicts.refines: It passes the criterion's test: it is one part, cause, case or means of its parent, narrower than the parent

weak-link.description: Related to the parent, but the link is indirect, or it restates the parent in other words instead of naming one part of it
weak-link.guidance: Say how it serves the parent, or narrow it to one part of the parent.

misplaced.description: It does not belong under its parent
misplaced.guidance: Move it under the node it belongs to.

rules.description: A node's children are separate: none counts towards another

semantic.rubric: Judge the item's children as a set. If the criterion names a kind of child, judge only those and ignore the rest. Children overlap when two state the same thing, or when one counts towards or contains another. Children that share a topic, a team or a budget are separate if neither counts towards the other. Whether one child has to wait for another is a different question: ignore it.

overlapping.description: Two children state the same thing, or one counts towards or contains another
overlapping.guidance: Merge them, sharpen the boundary between them, or nest the narrower one under the broader one.

rules.description: A node's children are separate results, not steps in a sequence

semantic.rubric: Judge the item's children as a set. If the criterion names a kind of child, judge only those and ignore the rest. Children are dependent when one cannot start, or cannot succeed, until another is finished, so they are steps in a sequence rather than separate results. The order may be stated, or plain from the bodies. Children that help each other, or share a team or a budget, are independent when each could go ahead on its own. Overlap between children is a different question: ignore it.

verdicts.independent: Each child could go ahead on its own

dependent.description: One child has to be finished before another can start or succeed
dependent.guidance: Keep separate results as the children, and move the steps into a plan under the result they deliver.

rules.description: A node moves its parent forward, as a part of it or by driving it

semantic.rubric: Judge only how the item relates to its parent. The item ladders up when achieving or addressing it would move the parent forward, either because it is a part of the parent or because it drives the parent. The criterion says what moving forward means for these types. Something worthwhile in the same area that would not move the parent does not ladder up.

verdicts.ladders-up: Achieving it would move the parent forward, as a part of it or by driving it

loosely-related.description: Related to the parent, but the link is indirect or unclear, or it restates the parent in other words
loosely-related.guidance: Say how it moves the parent, or narrow it to one part or driver of the parent.

does-not-ladder-up.description: Achieving it would not move the parent forward
does-not-ladder-up.guidance: Move it under the node it does move, or drop it.

rules.description: A node serves every level above it, not only its parent

semantic.rubric: Follow the chain from the item through each ancestor to the top. Pass when the item, if achieved, serves every level as the criterion describes. Fail when it would serve its parent but ignore, or work against, the intent of a level above.
